reviews.text: 3d街机空战机制集大成者，从前作afterburn的模式上改进而来。飞机的鼠标操控取消了前作的无敌滚筒躲避，类似warthunder的街机操作模式，不过没有单独的横滚和俯仰（但游戏节奏非常之快，外加hitbox较大，没有也正常）。本作主角机相当于前作eagle机同时带了30机炮和导弹，机炮加了些许偏航角，所以在一定范围内不需要机头完全对敌就能开火命中。同时添加了rouge升级的要素，不过部分升级部件需要完成成就来解锁。 敌人波次来袭（数量大致相同，但每一局配置较为随机），规模越来越大。每完成两到三次波次切换场景，这时如果tech等级吃够了可以从3个随机升级选项里选择一个。敌人配置是在3d空战里比较典型的杂鱼机炮机，高级导弹机，王牌机（可变战斗机，机动强悍，会悬停和闪避导弹，有三层血。千万不要与其进入低速格斗，这是不可能的，尽量与其拉开距离后对头，同时发射导弹封闭走位），多部件强火力的护卫舰（上方有ciws，两侧有导弹，推荐从下方进攻），以及只有护卫舰导弹火力的空塔。 本作一局游戏时间较短，强度较高，机制非常爽快，适合没事时打一两局。同时有全球36小时内分数排名榜，可以尝试挑战。

我TM射爆啊啊啊！！！ 速度就是你的装甲，在战斗中保持速度！！！ 一开始不知道自带导弹，还以为要rouge出来才有，升级成AC-60MM机炮后无意中点射才发现是发射导弹 操作指南： 注意！本作的机体是固定装甲值设定，不像前作可以呼吸回血。 机体基础有三层装甲。 W：加速 S：减速 A：左移 D：右移 鼠标移动：控制机头朝向，有一定的延后性，若想灵活掉头，可以使用S减速配合鼠标，但要 在确保敌机在安全距离外； 鼠标右键：可以锁定敌机，会将你的机头朝向被锁定的敌机，并稍微拉近视野，提高你的弹道 收束； 有个rouge出来的技能叫（ICEMAN）在锁定的时候会有1秒左右的子弹时间； 因为本作取消了前作的无敌翻滚，导致回转性能下降，不过可以使用锁定配合AD左 右移动来回转机身，此操作慢于减速转身，并且视角锁定； 熟练后可以不锁定，只是瞄准敌机方向，配合AD位移，此时机腹朝向屏幕，通过侧 翻机身来快速回转。 鼠标左键/空格：长按机炮，点击发射导弹；敌机的导弹和无人机都是可以用机炮点掉的。 击毁敌机除了给游戏分数，敌机还会掉落残骸，以六个环绕的六边形图标显示，六边形会慢慢减少，要在其减少消失前飞到附近回收，回收残骸会增加左下角的（TECH 1 >>>>）科技槽，满了就会在回合间隙提供3个升级选项。 目前有三种机炮：1.基础款30MM机炮； 2.AC-60（60MM机炮）升级射程威力准度降射速； 3.GAU-20（20MM密集阵）泼水。 导弹升级目前就一个：IR-4，弹匣和备弹翻倍，不过单击一次发射两枚导弹。 机体升级：几个机体性能和操作性的升级，一个增加一层装甲的升级； MECHANIC升级：每次回收残骸除了科技点，还会回复部分装甲值，后续成就解锁 MECHANIC+回复效果加强；但是回复超过100%不会增加装甲层，而是将当前装甲 层提升超过100%，如150%，220%，且回复的装甲值会慢慢回落。 VECTOR升级：机体推进器升级为矢量喷口，提高机体灵活性，回转能力和悬停机 能。 天空塔BOSS：在其机库打开时攻击才有效，高速掠袭可以穿过无人机群，打了就跑，或者使用绕柱战术，不过容易被击中，因为速度慢了。 在天空塔的地图，在消灭杂兵机后，尽早摧毁天空塔，这样天空塔就不会发射自杀无人机。因为天空塔不会坠落，在打类似VF战机的ACE BOSS时可以将天空塔做掩体减速绕着天空塔打（秦王绕柱永远有用）。 天空塔顶部停机坪的扳手光标，吃掉回复100%装甲值，摧毁后中央机库中的残骸光标不会消失，吃掉后回复一层装甲，如果此时是3层装甲，会增加至4层装甲。 战舰BOSS：顶部舰炮威力等同自机的60MM重型机炮，命中2次摧毁1层装甲，两侧导弹发射器，1发摧毁1层装甲；推荐从底部，舰首，舰尾发起攻击，BOSS会倾斜舰体让舰炮射界瞄准你，尽量绕着打，舰炮的回转速度稍微慢于自机的回旋速度； 要摧毁3个部件战舰才会坠毁，战舰有5个部件：舰首，舰尾，左右导弹发射器，舰炮。 舰首，舰尾体积大，命中率高，导弹发射器在舰体侧面，可以高速掠袭扫射配合导弹摧毁， 不推荐攻击舰炮，舰炮呈圆盘状，侧面投影面积小，且容易形成对狙，攻顶命中率高，但是舰炮仰角有180°左右，同样危险。 VF战机BOSS：和自机一样3层装甲，攻击模式：机炮+导弹，引擎能够反转逆喷，回转性能十分优秀，机炮命中率较高，不要与其低速狗斗对射，敌机命中率比你高；离开距离，保持回旋，时不时锁定一下，调整机头方向，保持导弹的发射，确保总有部分导弹在追踪BOSS，不要给BOSS全力攻击你的机会，有了安全距离，在其没有瞄准你时，快速减速回转掉头，提速，全力发射导弹，让导弹干扰其飞行，进入机炮射程后，机炮配合导弹攻击，总有一种攻击能命中。
Play this while blasting your favorite Ace Combat music.

Game looks promissing, but as of now V0,85 still no recommendation from me! 1. Scraps are disapearing way to fast. Nothing has been done to mitigate this. 2. Frigates and Towers do release rockets/drones when they get destroyed, even if they did that allready shortly before destruction -> Why? 3. There is no other way to get a live back then flying through a rater narrow slot in the towers. Most of the time either crashing into it because of speed or eating a rocket from fighters because of slowing down. 4. Upgradeprocess is tedious, first because of point 1 (scraps are needed for upgrades) and second there is no option to reroll the choices presented. This can be especially frustrating when the first choices of a run contain no weapon upgrade at all! Have fun with the basic weaponry up to wave 4! Encountering at least one or two frigates -> watch your score get overtaken by a snail in reverse! 5. New BS that has been introduced -> not enough enemies to recieve ONE update through waves 1-3. At least enemies do not aim to ram anymore.

This is a good game suffering from bad balance. Its worth it to get it, but there's some things you need to know before you get into it. I'll list everything as Pro's and Con's. Pro's: -The game looks and feels awesome, I love the art style so much. -When you do things, it always looks cooler than it actually is. -The game is VERY re-playable due to enemy variety and upgrade variety. -The sound design is a 10/10. -Models are also a 10/10. -Unique enemy types I haven't seen before in games like it. -The UI is minimalistic while easily displaying all necessary information. -The hold right click auto aim mechanic is a 20/10 and a life saver. Use the HELL out of it. _________________________________________________________________________________ Con's: -Missiles. Oh god the missiles. The enemy spams them so much and they do so much damage. The devs need to either make them rarer, or have variations of missiles. Like one missile type is spammable but doesn't do as much damage, and the other is a heavy missile that is rarer, but does a lot of damage. -Warships are the most broken op thing ever. They have a dash option to dodge your missiles, a giant aimbot auto-cannon that fires every five seconds or so, 6 missiles every 15 seconds, and can only be killed through destroying three parts of the body, or two and the gun. The part damage thing is a cool idea, but they put it on the most OP enemy in the game. Solution to fix the warship: Reduce accuracy of the auto-cannon depending on range, decrease missiles to four, and make the dash weaker. The part damage is cool, keep that. -There's slow bombs that can be deployed by special units. And you just... never see those bombs. You see them like once or twice per play session. Buff their speed, and make them more common please. -What the hell is tech level? This is never explained in the game and I have never noticed any difference when it leveled up. PLEASE make a tutorial for this game. -Why does a futuristic fighter jet not have deploy-able flares for missile defense? You're just at the enemies mercy with their missiles. Sure you can shoot the missiles, but you have to be flying at it to do that. Please at least add flares as an upgrade on a cooldown like the missiles. -Your missiles should target the enemy closest to your mouse, not closest to your plane. There's probably some counter point to be made here, but the missiles just feel janky because of it. -I WANNA DO THE SAME THING THAT THE ADVANCED FIGHTERS DO AND GO PSEUDO GUNDAM MODE WAAAAH (Not an actual con, I just wanna do that lmao)

[h3]Small but fun, fast paced, roguelite-ish air combat game.[/h3] [b]TLDR Review: Worth it on a sale. [/b] [b]Description:[/b] You start each run in an un-upgraded aircraft, armed with both guns and missiles. Killing an enemy drops scraps, which heal you for a small amount but also contribute to your tech-level. When you reach a new tech-level, you get to pick one out of three upgrades. Upgrades can affect the type of gun or missiles you have, the performance of your aircraft or it's durability. Enemies consist of nimble ones like fighters, interceptors and mech-aircraft hybrids called wing leaders, to less nimble or even stationary ones like frigates, stations and outposts. Runs are randomized every day, you compete for leaderboard position. Each run is quite short, either 8 waves or 12 waves at the moment. [b]Pros:[/b] Intuitive drop in gameplay, but has some depth under the hood (Knowing some basics about aerial combat actually does help, despite using an arcadey, science fiction-y flight model). Runs are quite action-packed and there is practically zero downtime. Upgrades are generally meaningful and can be directly felt in gameplay. Leaderboard competition means you always have a new goal in mind everyday. A picture perfect example of easy to learn, difficult to master. Hella fun but does have some minor issues. It's fast, it's fun, and it reminds me a lot of Ace Combat. The game is basically just one long fight to see how long you can last like the old retro-arcade games. And the game gives you plenty of targets that go up in lethality as you play from weak Viper jets that can go down in one missile to aggressive space ships with missiles to spare. This isn't a game you play to see the end of a story (btw there's no story, it's just ALL gameplay) this is a game you play to get the top score on. And I love it. That said, there are a few minor issues with the game. For one, you have a lives system, if you take too much damage, you will lose a life. You can mitigate this by, well, either upgrading your jet or getting gud but I did notice that no where on the HUD did it remind you how many lives you still had. Now, you COULD argue that this encourages the player not to play recklessly, but you could also argue the opposite for it too considering if we can't see how many times we're allowed to mess up, we'll forget how we've messed up already and die before we realize we're out of lives. There's also kind of an issue where enemy missiles have a tendency to be inconsistently accurate. Some enemy missiles you can strafe around without worry, others will be on you like bloodhounds. It wouldn't be so bad if maybe we had unique target indicators to tell which were threats and which weren't, but since all missiles have the same indicator, you don't have much choice but to treat them all like a threat. And another gripe I have, the game does not tell you when you're low on health. I mean sure, it's there on your HUD but most other fighter jet games have an alarm or something that goes off to warn you that you're in serious danger and need to start playing more cautiously. Top Dog, for whatever reason, doesn't have that. And in a super-fast paced game, you need to keep your eyes on the ball so having to check every time you cut it close how much health you have is uhh... not what I would call good game design. Graphically, the game is nothing to write home about, but that's no big deal. This game was designed first and foremost to be fun and they accomplished that with flying colours. I do however don't care much for the music (of which as far as I've played only really plays on the main menu). There's also no customisation, I guess due to the fact that some of the upgrades to change the look of your jet. Which is fair enough. Overall, 9/10. Super solid game with some minor but otherwise easy-to-get-around issues.
